Management Summary

Threagile toolkit was used to model the architecture of "Web Shop on Kubernetes" and derive risks by analyzing the components and data flows. The risks identified during this analysis are shown in the following chapters. Identified risks during threat modeling do not necessarily mean that the vulnerability associated with this risk actually exists: it is more to be seen as a list of potential risks and threats, which should be individually reviewed and reduced by removing false positives. For the remaining risks it should be checked in the design and implementation of "Web Shop on Kubernetes" whether the mitigation advices have been applied or not.

Each risk finding references a chapter of the OWASP ASVS (Application Security Verification Standard) audit checklist. The OWASP ASVS checklist should be considered as an inspiration by architects and developers to further harden the application in a Defense-in-Depth approach. Additionally, for each risk finding a link towards a matching OWASP Cheat Sheet or similar with technical details about how to implement a mitigation is given.

In total 35 initial risks in 20 categories have been identified during the threat modeling process:

Impact Analysis of the Initial Risks

The most prevalent impacts of the 35 initial risks (distributed over 20 risk categories) are (taking the severity ratings into account and using the highest for each category):

Elevated Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): 1 Initial Risk, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to access individual victim sessions and steal or modify user data.
Elevated Missing Cloud Hardening: 1 Initial Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Very High impact
If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might access cloud components in an unintended way.
Elevated Missing Hardening: 3 Initial Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to easier attack high-value targets.
Elevated Missing Network Policy: 2 Initial Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who compromise any pod of the cluster might move on to the workloads of the namespace and their data, or, from a pod of the namespace, to anything it can reach.

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access sensitive services or files of network-reachable components by modifying outgoing calls of affected components.

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to deeply persist in the target system by executing code in deployed containers.
Medium Container Platform Escape: 1 Initial Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
If this risk is unmitigated, attackers which have successfully compromised a container (via other vulnerabilities) might be able to deeply persist in the target system by executing code in many deployed containers and the container platform itself.
Medium Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF): 1 Initial Risk, exploitation likelihood is Very Likely with Low impact

Medium Kubernetes API Write Access: 1 Initial Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with High impact

If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to easier attack high-value targets.

Medium Missing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): 1 Initial Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact

Medium Missing Network Policy: 2 Initial Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who compromise any pod of the cluster might move on to the workloads of the namespace and their data, or, from a pod of the namespace, to anything it can reach.

Application Overview

Business Criticality

The overall business criticality of "Web Shop on Kubernetes" was rated as:

  • archive
  • operational
  • important
  • critical
  • mission-critical

Business Overview

An online shop whose services run in a managed Kubernetes cluster.

Technical Overview

The shop's services run in namespaces of one cluster on a shared node pool. An ingress controller takes the traffic of the customers, a GitOps operator applies the deployments, and a node agent collects the logs.

STRIDE Classification of Identified Risks

This chapter clusters and classifies the risks by STRIDE categories: in total 35 potential risks have been identified during the threat modeling process.

Spoofing 3 risks

Spoofing - Authenticity

Medium Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Very Likely with Low impact
When a web application is accessed via web protocols Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) risks might arise.
Medium Long-Lived Credentials: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Passwords of service accounts, API keys and personal access tokens stay valid for months or for good. Once one leaks, from a repository, a log, a build system or a laptop, it lets anyone in until someone notices and rotates it.
Medium Missing Identity Store: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
The modeled architecture does not contain an identity store, which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks).

Tampering 15 risks

Tampering - Integrity

Elevated Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
For each web application Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) risks might arise. In terms of the overall risk level take other applications running on the same domain into account as well.
Elevated Missing Cloud Hardening: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Very High impact
Cloud components should be hardened according to the cloud vendor best practices. This affects their configuration, auditing, and further areas.
Elevated Missing Hardening: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
Technical assets with a Relative Attacker Attractiveness (RAA) value of 55 % or higher should be explicitly hardened taking best practices and vendor hardening guides into account.
Elevated SQL/NoSQL-Injection: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Very Likely with Medium impact
When a database is accessed via database access protocols SQL/NoSQL-Injection risks might arise. The risk rating depends on the sensitivity technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Medium Container Base Image Backdooring: 8/8 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with High impact
When a technical asset is built using container technologies, Base Image Backdooring risks might arise where base images and other layers used contain vulnerable components or backdoors.
Medium Missing Build Infrastructure: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
The modeled architecture does not contain a build infrastructure (devops-client, sourcecode-repo, build-pipeline, etc.), which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks). If the architecture contains custom-developed parts, the pipeline where code gets developed and built needs to be part of the model.
Medium Missing Hardening: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
Technical assets with a Relative Attacker Attractiveness (RAA) value of 55 % or higher should be explicitly hardened taking best practices and vendor hardening guides into account.

Repudiation 0 risks

Repudiation - Non-repudiability

No risks were identified.

Information Disclosure 5 risks

Information disclosure - Confidentiality

Elevated Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF): 4/4 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
When a server system (i.e. not a client) is accessing other server systems via typical web protocols Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) or Local-File-Inclusion (LFI) or Remote-File-Inclusion (RFI) risks might arise.
Medium Missing Vault (Secret Storage): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
In order to avoid the risk of secret leakage via config files (when attacked through vulnerabilities being able to read files like Path-Traversal and others), it is best practice to use a separate hardened process with proper authentication, authorization, and audit logging to access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.). This component is usually some kind of Vault.

Denial of Service 0 risks

Denial of service - Availability

No risks were identified.

Elevation of Privilege 12 risks

Elevation of privilege - Authorization

Elevated Missing Network Policy: 2/2 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Without network policies, every pod of a Kubernetes cluster can reach the pods of a namespace, and its pods can reach the rest of the cluster and beyond: the namespace separates names, not traffic.
Medium Container Platform Escape: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Container platforms are especially interesting targets for attackers as they host big parts of a containerized runtime infrastructure. When not configured and operated with security best practices in mind, attackers might exploit a vulnerability inside an container and escape towards the platform as highly privileged users. These scenarios might give attackers capabilities to attack every other container as owning the container platform (via container escape attacks) equals to owning every container.
Medium Kubernetes API Write Access: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with High impact
A workload whose service account may change resources through the API of its cluster, even narrowly, like creating pods, reading secrets or patching deployments, hands that power to whoever compromises the workload: a pod created with a mounted host path, or a secret read, opens the rest of the cluster.
Medium Missing Identity Propagation: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Technical assets (especially multi-tenant systems), which usually process data for end users should authorize every request based on the identity of the end user when the data flow is authenticated (i.e. non-public). For DevOps usages at least the identity of a service account or a workload is required.
Medium Missing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Technical assets (especially multi-tenant systems) should authenticate incoming requests with multi-factor (MFA) authentication when the asset processes or stores highly sensitive data (in terms of confidentiality, integrity, and availability) and is accessed by humans.
Medium Missing Network Policy: 2/2 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Without network policies, every pod of a Kubernetes cluster can reach the pods of a namespace, and its pods can reach the rest of the cluster and beyond: the namespace separates names, not traffic.
Medium Missing Network Segmentation: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Highly sensitive assets and/or data stores residing in the same network segment than other lower sensitive assets (like webservers or content management systems etc.) should be better protected by a network segmentation trust-boundary.
Medium Mixed Targets on Shared Runtime: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Different attacker targets (like frontend and backend/datastore components) should not be running on the same shared (underlying) runtime.
Medium Privileged Workload: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with High impact
A workload that runs as a privileged container, mounts a path of its node or shares the node's network, process or IPC namespace is not contained by its container: whoever controls the workload controls the node, the other workloads on it and the credentials of the node's kubelet.
Low Missing Network Segmentation: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Highly sensitive assets and/or data stores residing in the same network segment than other lower sensitive assets (like webservers or content management systems etc.) should be better protected by a network segmentation trust-boundary.
Low Unnecessary Technical Asset: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Low impact
When a technical asset does not process any data assets, this is an indicator for an unnecessary technical asset (or for an incomplete model). This is also the case if the asset has no communication links (either outgoing or incoming).

Assignment by Function

This chapter clusters and assigns the risks by functions which are most likely able to check and mitigate them: in total 35 potential risks have been identified during the threat modeling process.

Business Side 1 risk

Business

Medium Missing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Apply an authentication method to the technical asset protecting highly sensitive data via multi-factor authentication for human users.

Architecture 5 risks

Architecture

Medium Missing Build Infrastructure: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Include the build infrastructure in the model.
Medium Missing Identity Propagation: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
When processing requests for end users if possible authorize in the backend against the propagated identity of the end user. This can be achieved in passing JWTs or similar tokens and checking them in the backend services, and model the link with the identity end-user. For DevOps usages pass at least the identity of a service account or a workload.
Medium Missing Identity Store: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Include an identity store in the model if the application has a login.
Medium Missing Vault (Secret Storage): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Consider using a Vault (Secret Storage) to securely store and access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.).
Low Unnecessary Technical Asset: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Low impact
Try to avoid using technical assets that do not process or store anything.

Development 7 risks

Development

Elevated Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
Try to encode all values sent back to the browser and also handle DOM-manipulations in a safe way to avoid DOM-based XSS. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.
Elevated SQL/NoSQL-Injection: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Very Likely with Medium impact
Try to use parameter binding to be safe from injection vulnerabilities. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.
Elevated Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF): 4/4 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
Try to avoid constructing the outgoing target URL with caller controllable values. Alternatively use a mapping (whitelist) when accessing outgoing URLs instead of creating them including caller controllable values. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.
Medium Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Very Likely with Low impact
Try to use anti-CSRF tokens ot the double-submit patterns (at least for logged-in requests). When your authentication scheme depends on cookies (like session or token cookies), consider marking them with the same-site flag. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

Operations 22 risks

Operations

Elevated Missing Cloud Hardening: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Very High impact
Apply hardening of all cloud components and services, taking special care to follow the individual risk descriptions (which depend on the cloud provider tags in the model).
Elevated Missing Hardening: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
Try to apply all hardening best practices (like CIS benchmarks, OWASP recommendations, vendor recommendations, DevSec Hardening Framework, DBSAT for Oracle databases, and others).
Elevated Missing Network Policy: 2/2 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Deny all ingress and egress traffic of the namespace by default with a network policy, allow only the traffic that its workloads need, by namespace and pod labels and ports, and make sure the network plugin of the cluster enforces network policies. Model the namespace with the network_policy ingress-and-egress once they are in place.
Medium Container Base Image Backdooring: 8/8 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with High impact
Apply hardening of all container infrastructures (see for example the CIS-Benchmarks for Docker and Kubernetes and the Docker Bench for Security). Use only trusted base images of the original vendors, verify digital signatures and apply image creation best practices. Also consider using Google's Distroless base images or otherwise very small base images. Regularly execute container image scans with tools checking the layers for vulnerable components.
Medium Container Platform Escape: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Apply hardening of all container infrastructures.
Medium Kubernetes API Write Access: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with High impact
Give the workload a service account of its own, bound to a role in its namespace with only the verbs and resources it uses (no create on pods, no get on secrets, no wildcards), disable the mounting of its token where it does not call the API, and leave changes to the cluster to the deployment pipeline or an operator on nodes of its own.
Medium Long-Lived Credentials: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Replace static secrets between services with a workload identity issued by the platform (cloud IAM roles, Kubernetes service account tokens, SPIFFE), or with short-lived tokens obtained through OAuth 2.0 client credentials or token exchange, and model the link with the identity workload or the authentication short-lived-token. Where a long-lived secret remains, keep it in a vault, scope it narrowly, rotate it automatically and detect its use from unexpected places.
Medium Missing Hardening: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with Medium impact
Try to apply all hardening best practices (like CIS benchmarks, OWASP recommendations, vendor recommendations, DevSec Hardening Framework, DBSAT for Oracle databases, and others).
Medium Missing Network Policy: 2/2 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Likely with High impact
Deny all ingress and egress traffic of the namespace by default with a network policy, allow only the traffic that its workloads need, by namespace and pod labels and ports, and make sure the network plugin of the cluster enforces network policies. Model the namespace with the network_policy ingress-and-egress once they are in place.
Medium Missing Network Segmentation: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Apply a network segmentation trust-boundary around the highly sensitive assets and/or data stores.
Medium Mixed Targets on Shared Runtime: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Use separate runtime environments for running different target components or apply similar separation styles to prevent load- or breach-related problems originating from one more attacker-facing asset impacts also the other more critical rated backend/datastore assets.
Medium Privileged Workload: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with High impact
Run the workload unprivileged, as a non-root user with a read-only root file system, without host paths, host namespaces and added capabilities, and enforce the restricted Pod Security Standard on its namespace. A workload that must stay privileged, like a node agent, belongs on nodes of its own and deserves the hardening of the node itself.
Low Missing Network Segmentation: 3/3 unmitigated Risks, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
Apply a network segmentation trust-boundary around the highly sensitive assets and/or data stores.

RAA Analysis

For each technical asset the "Relative Attacker Attractiveness" (RAA) value was calculated in percent. The higher the RAA, the more interesting it is for an attacker to compromise the asset. The calculation algorithm takes the sensitivity ratings and quantities of stored and processed data into account as well as the communication links of the technical asset. Neighbouring assets to high-value RAA targets might receive an increase in their RAA value when they have a communication link towards that target ("Pivoting-Factor").

The following lists all technical assets sorted by their RAA value from highest (most attacker attractive) to lowest. This list can be used to prioritize on efforts relevant for the most attacker-attractive technical assets:

Potential Model Failures 4 of 4 unmitigated

This chapter lists potential model failures where not all relevant assets have been modeled or the model might itself contain inconsistencies. Each potential model failure should be checked in the model against the architecture design:

Medium Missing Build Infrastructure: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
The modeled architecture does not contain a build infrastructure (devops-client, sourcecode-repo, build-pipeline, etc.), which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks). If the architecture contains custom-developed parts, the pipeline where code gets developed and built needs to be part of the model.
Medium Missing Identity Store: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
The modeled architecture does not contain an identity store, which might be the risk of a model missing critical assets (and thus not seeing their risks).
Medium Missing Vault (Secret Storage): 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Medium impact
In order to avoid the risk of secret leakage via config files (when attacked through vulnerabilities being able to read files like Path-Traversal and others), it is best practice to use a separate hardened process with proper authentication, authorization, and audit logging to access config secrets (like credentials, private keys, client certificates, etc.). This component is usually some kind of Vault.
Low Unnecessary Technical Asset: 1/1 unmitigated Risk, exploitation likelihood is Unlikely with Low impact
When a technical asset does not process any data assets, this is an indicator for an unnecessary technical asset (or for an incomplete model). This is also the case if the asset has no communication links (either outgoing or incoming).

In-scope web applications.

False Positives

Description

Cloud components should be hardened according to the cloud vendor best practices. This affects their configuration, auditing, and further areas.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might access cloud components in an unintended way.

Detection Logic

In-scope cloud components (either residing in cloud trust boundaries or more specifically tagged with cloud provider types).

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.

False Positives

Cloud components not running parts of the target architecture can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Apply hardening of all cloud components and services, taking special care to follow the individual risk descriptions (which depend on the cloud provider tags in the model).

For Amazon Web Services (AWS): Follow the CIS Benchmark for Amazon Web Services (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "PacBot", "CloudSploit", "CloudMapper", "ScoutSuite", or "Prowler AWS CIS Benchmark Tool").
For EC2 and other servers running Amazon Linux, follow the CIS Benchmark for Amazon Linux and switch to IMDSv2.
For S3 buckets follow the Security Best Practices for Amazon S3 at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/security-best-practices.html to avoid accidental leakage.
Also take a look at some of these tools: https://github.com/toniblyx/my-arsenal-of-aws-security-tools

For Microsoft Azure: Follow the CIS Benchmark for Microsoft Azure (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "CloudSploit" or "ScoutSuite").

For Google Cloud Platform: Follow the CIS Benchmark for Google Cloud Computing Platform (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "CloudSploit" or "ScoutSuite").

For Oracle Cloud Platform: Follow the hardening best practices (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "CloudSploit").

Missing Network Policy Elevated 2/2 unmitigated Risks

missing-network-policy

STRIDEElevation of Privilege

FunctionOperations
ActionNetwork Segmentation of Namespaces
ASVS chapterV1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements
Cheat sheetKubernetes_Security_Cheat_Sheet
ReferencesOWASP K05:2025 Missing Network Segmentation Controls; OWASP A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration

Description

Without network policies, every pod of a Kubernetes cluster can reach the pods of a namespace, and its pods can reach the rest of the cluster and beyond: the namespace separates names, not traffic.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who compromise any pod of the cluster might move on to the workloads of the namespace and their data, or, from a pod of the namespace, to anything it can reach.

Detection Logic

Execution environment trust boundaries (Kubernetes namespaces) whose network_policy is none, ingress or egress, holding in-scope technical assets that process or store data rated at least as confidential or critical. Namespaces whose network policy is not modelled are skipped.

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the most sensitive technical asset in the namespace. The attack is likely when incoming traffic is not restricted, and unlikely when only outgoing traffic is not.

False Positives

Namespaces whose traffic a service mesh restricts by default, with authorization policies that allow only the intended callers, can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Deny all ingress and egress traffic of the namespace by default with a network policy, allow only the traffic that its workloads need, by namespace and pod labels and ports, and make sure the network plugin of the cluster enforces network policies. Model the namespace with the network_policy ingress-and-egress once they are in place.

Check

Description

When a server system (i.e. not a client) is accessing other server systems via typical web protocols Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) or Local-File-Inclusion (LFI) or Remote-File-Inclusion (RFI) risks might arise.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access sensitive services or files of network-reachable components by modifying outgoing calls of affected components.

Detection Logic

In-scope non-client systems accessing (using outgoing communication links) targets with either HTTP or HTTPS protocol.

Risk Rating

The risk rating (low or medium) depends on the sensitivity of the data assets receivable via web protocols from targets within the same network trust-boundary as well on the sensitivity of the data assets receivable via web protocols from the target asset itself. Also for cloud-based environments the exploitation impact is at least medium, as cloud backend services can be attacked via SSRF.

False Positives

Servers not sending outgoing web requests can be considered as false positives after review.

Mitigation

Try to avoid constructing the outgoing target URL with caller controllable values. Alternatively use a mapping (whitelist) when accessing outgoing URLs instead of creating them including caller controllable values. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

Description

When a technical asset is built using container technologies, Base Image Backdooring risks might arise where base images and other layers used contain vulnerable components or backdoors.

See for example: https://techcrunch.com/2018/06/15/tainted-crypto-mining-containers-pulled-from-docker-hub/

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to deeply persist in the target system by executing code in deployed containers.

Detection Logic

In-scope technical assets running as containers, other than external entities. To track the risks of all containers at once, use the risk tracking key container-baseimage-backdooring@*.

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets.

False Positives

Fully trusted (i.e. reviewed and cryptographically signed or similar) base images of containers can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Apply hardening of all container infrastructures (see for example the CIS-Benchmarks for Docker and Kubernetes and the Docker Bench for Security). Use only trusted base images of the original vendors, verify digital signatures and apply image creation best practices. Also consider using Google's Distroless base images or otherwise very small base images. Regularly execute container image scans with tools checking the layers for vulnerable components.

Description

Container platforms are especially interesting targets for attackers as they host big parts of a containerized runtime infrastructure. When not configured and operated with security best practices in mind, attackers might exploit a vulnerability inside an container and escape towards the platform as highly privileged users. These scenarios might give attackers capabilities to attack every other container as owning the container platform (via container escape attacks) equals to owning every container.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers which have successfully compromised a container (via other vulnerabilities) might be able to deeply persist in the target system by executing code in many deployed containers and the container platform itself.

Detection Logic

In-scope container platforms.

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.

False Positives

Container platforms not running parts of the target architecture can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Apply hardening of all container infrastructures. <p>See for example the CIS-Benchmarks for Docker and Kubernetes as well as the Docker Bench for Security ( https://github.com/docker/docker-bench-security ) or InSpec Checks for Docker and Kubernetes ( https://github.com/dev-sec/cis-docker-benchmark and https://github.com/dev-sec/cis-kubernetes-benchmark ). Use only trusted base images, verify digital signatures and apply image creation best practices. Also consider using Google's Distroless</i> base images or otherwise very small base images. Apply namespace isolation and nod affinity to separate pods from each other in terms of access and nodes the same style as you separate data.

cross-site-request-forgery

STRIDESpoofing

FunctionDevelopment

Cheat sheetCross-Site_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet
ReferencesOWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control

Description

When a web application is accessed via web protocols Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) risks might arise.

Impact

If this risk remains unmitigated, attackers might be able to trick logged-in victim users into unwanted actions within the web application by visiting an attacker controlled web site.

Detection Logic

In-scope web applications accessed via typical web access protocols by a caller used by humans or a browser, directly or through technical assets forwarding the traffic, like load balancers, reverse proxies and WAFs. Requests of other callers, like a backend or a batch job, come from no browser a forged request could use, and are skipped.

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the integrity rating of the data sent across the communication link. The attack is very likely, likely for DevOps usage, and unlikely when the link is authenticated with a token (token, short-lived-token or long-lived-token), which a browser does not send on its own like a cookie.

False Positives

Web applications passing the authentication state via custom headers instead of cookies can eventually be false positives; model their links with a token authentication. Clients used by humans that are no browser and render no web content, like a command-line tool, can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Try to use anti-CSRF tokens ot the double-submit patterns (at least for logged-in requests). When your authentication scheme depends on cookies (like session or token cookies), consider marking them with the same-site flag. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

Check

Description

A workload whose service account may change resources through the API of its cluster, even narrowly, like creating pods, reading secrets or patching deployments, hands that power to whoever compromises the workload: a pod created with a mounted host path, or a secret read, opens the rest of the cluster.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who compromise the workload might run their own workloads in the cluster, read its secrets and take over the other workloads and their data.

Detection Logic

Communication links that are not readonly and not process-local to a container-platform technical asset from a technical asset that is not used by humans, where either is in scope. Links of devops usage, like deployments, are skipped.

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the most sensitive of the platform, the workload and the technical assets sharing a runtime with the workload. The attack is likely when the workload is on the internet or talks to the internet, and unlikely otherwise.

False Positives

Operators and controllers whose job is to change the cluster, running on nodes of their own with roles scoped to what they manage, can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Give the workload a service account of its own, bound to a role in its namespace with only the verbs and resources it uses (no create on pods, no get on secrets, no wildcards), disable the mounting of its token where it does not call the API, and leave changes to the cluster to the deployment pipeline or an operator on nodes of its own.

Check

Cheat sheetSecrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet
ReferencesOWASP A07:2025 Authentication Failures; OWASP NHI7:2025 Long-Lived Secrets; OWASP NHI2:2025 Secret Leakage

Description

Passwords of service accounts, API keys and personal access tokens stay valid for months or for good. Once one leaks, from a repository, a log, a build system or a laptop, it lets anyone in until someone notices and rotates it.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who find a leaked secret might use it for a long time to access the target with the permissions of the caller.

Detection Logic

In-scope technical assets processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with an incoming communication link that is not process-local and is authenticated with long-lived-token, or with credentials by a caller not used by humans, unless the identity of the link is workload. Links authenticated with token are skipped, as the lifetime of the token is not modelled.

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed or stored by the target. The attack is likely when the caller is on the internet, is used by humans or calls across a network trust boundary, where secrets leak more easily, and unlikely otherwise.

False Positives

Secrets that are rotated automatically within hours can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Replace static secrets between services with a workload identity issued by the platform (cloud IAM roles, Kubernetes service account tokens, SPIFFE), or with short-lived tokens obtained through OAuth 2.0 client credentials or token exchange, and model the link with the identity workload or the authentication short-lived-token. Where a long-lived secret remains, keep it in a vault, scope it narrowly, rotate it automatically and detect its use from unexpected places.

Missing Identity Propagation Medium 1/1 unmitigated Risk

missing-identity-propagation

STRIDEElevation of Privilege
CWECWE 284
FunctionArchitecture
ActionIdentity Propagation and Resource-based Authorization
ASVS chapterV4 - Access Control Verification Requirements
Cheat sheetAccess_Control_Cheat_Sheet
ReferencesOWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control; OWASP API1:2023 Broken Object Level Authorization

Description

Technical assets (especially multi-tenant systems), which usually process data for end users should authorize every request based on the identity of the end user when the data flow is authenticated (i.e. non-public). For DevOps usages at least the identity of a service account or a workload is required.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access or modify foreign data after a successful compromise of a component within the system due to missing resource-based authorization checks.

Detection Logic

In-scope service-like technical assets which usually process data based on end user requests, if authenticated (i.e. non-public), should authorize incoming requests based on the propagated end user identity when their rating is sensitive. This is especially the case for all multi-tenant assets (there even less-sensitive rated ones). DevOps usages are exempted from this risk.

Risk Rating

The risk rating (medium or high) depends on the confidentiality, integrity, and availability rating of the technical asset.

False Positives

Technical assets which do not process requests regarding functionality or data linked to end-users (customers) can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

When processing requests for end users if possible authorize in the backend against the propagated identity of the end user. This can be achieved in passing JWTs or similar tokens and checking them in the backend services, and model the link with the identity end-user. For DevOps usages pass at least the identity of a service account or a workload.

Description

Technical assets (especially multi-tenant systems) should authenticate incoming requests with multi-factor (MFA) authentication when the asset processes or stores highly sensitive data (in terms of confidentiality, integrity, and availability) and is accessed by humans.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers might be able to access or modify highly sensitive data without strong authentication.

Detection Logic

In-scope technical assets (except load-balancer, reverse-proxy, waf, ids, and ips) should authenticate incoming requests via multi-factor authentication (MFA) when the asset processes or stores highly sensitive data (in terms of confidentiality, integrity, and availability) and is accessed by a client used by a human user. Links over industrial control protocols that cannot authenticate are left to the insecure-control-protocol rule.

Risk Rating

medium

False Positives

Technical assets which do not process requests regarding functionality or data linked to end-users (customers) can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Apply an authentication method to the technical asset protecting highly sensitive data via multi-factor authentication for human users.

ReferencesOWASP A06:2025 Insecure Design

Description

Highly sensitive assets and/or data stores residing in the same network segment than other lower sensitive assets (like webservers or content management systems etc.) should be better protected by a network segmentation trust-boundary.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers successfully attacking other components of the system might have an easy path towards more valuable targets, as they are not separated by network segmentation.

Detection Logic

In-scope technical assets with high sensitivity and RAA values as well as data stores when surrounded by assets (without a network trust-boundary in-between) which are of type client-system, web-server, web-application, cms, web-service-rest, web-service-soap, build-pipeline, sourcecode-repository, monitoring, or similar and there is no direct connection between these (hence no requirement to be so close to each other).

Risk Rating

Default is low risk. The risk is increased to medium when the asset missing the trust-boundary protection is rated as strictly-confidential or mission-critical.

False Positives

When all assets within the network segmentation trust-boundary are hardened and protected to the same extend as if all were containing/processing highly sensitive data.

Mitigation

Apply a network segmentation trust-boundary around the highly sensitive assets and/or data stores.

This component is usually some kind of Vault.

False Positives

Mitigation

Description

Different attacker targets (like frontend and backend/datastore components) should not be running on the same shared (underlying) runtime.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers successfully attacking other components of the system might have an easy path towards more valuable targets, as they are running on the same shared runtime.

Detection Logic

Shared runtime running technical assets of different trust-boundaries is at risk. Also mixing backend/datastore with frontend components on the same shared runtime is considered a risk.

Risk Rating

The risk rating (low or medium) depends on the confidentiality, integrity, and availability rating of the technical asset running on the shared runtime.

False Positives

When all assets running on the shared runtime are hardened and protected to the same extend as if all were containing/processing highly sensitive data.

Mitigation

Use separate runtime environments for running different target components or apply similar separation styles to prevent load- or breach-related problems originating from one more attacker-facing asset impacts also the other more critical rated backend/datastore assets.

Privileged Workload Medium 1/1 unmitigated Risk

privileged-workload

STRIDEElevation of Privilege
CWECWE 250
FunctionOperations
ActionUnprivileged Workloads
ASVS chapterV1 - Architecture, Design and Threat Modeling Requirements
Cheat sheetKubernetes_Security_Cheat_Sheet
ReferencesOWASP K01:2025 Insecure Workload Configurations; OWASP A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration

Description

A workload that runs as a privileged container, mounts a path of its node or shares the node's network, process or IPC namespace is not contained by its container: whoever controls the workload controls the node, the other workloads on it and the credentials of the node's kubelet.

Impact

If this risk is unmitigated, attackers who compromise the workload might take over its node and from there the other workloads of the shared runtime and their data, and possibly the cluster.

Detection Logic

In-scope technical assets that are privileged (the field privileged), rated by what runs on the same shared runtimes.

Risk Rating

The risk rating depends on the most sensitive of the workload and the technical assets sharing a runtime with it, at least medium as the node itself is at stake. The attack is likely when the workload is on the internet or talks to the internet, and unlikely otherwise.

False Positives

Workloads that are privileged by design and run alone on dedicated nodes, like the agents of the platform, can be considered as false positives after individual review.

Mitigation

Run the workload unprivileged, as a non-root user with a read-only root file system, without host paths, host namespaces and added capabilities, and enforce the restricted Pod Security Standard on its namespace. A workload that must stay privileged, like a node agent, belongs on nodes of its own and deserves the hardening of the node itself.

Threagile (see threagile.io for more details) is an open-source toolkit for agile threat modeling, created by Christian Schneider (christian-schneider.net): It allows to model an architecture with its assets in an agile fashion as a YAML file directly inside the IDE. Upon execution of the Threagile toolkit all standard risk rules (as well as individual custom rules if present) are checked against the architecture model. At the time the Threagile toolkit was executed on the model input file the following risk rules were checked:

Risk ruleSTRIDEDescriptionDetectionRating
Accidental Secret Leak
accidental-secret-leak		Information DisclosureSourcecode repositories (including their histories) as well as artifact registries can accidentally contain secrets like checked-in or packaged-in passwords, API tokens, certificates, crypto keys, etc.In-scope sourcecode repositories and artifact registries.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Code Backdooring
code-backdooring		TamperingFor each build pipeline component Code Backdooring risks might arise where attackers compromise the build pipeline in order to let backdoored artifacts be shipped into production. Aside from direct code backdooring this includes backdooring of dependencies and even of more lower-level build infrastructure, like backdooring compilers (similar to what the XcodeGhost malware did) or dependencies.In-scope development relevant technical assets which are either accessed by out-of-scope unmanaged developer clients and/or are directly accessed by any kind of internet-located (non-VPN) component or are themselves directly located on the internet.The risk rating depends on the confidentiality and integrity rating of the code being handled and deployed as well as the placement/calling of this technical asset on/from the internet.
Confused Deputy Agent
confused-deputy-agent		Elevation of PrivilegeAn AI agent that acts for its users but reaches data and tools with an identity of its own, a service account or a workload, can do for any user what the agent may do for all of them. The targets check the agent, not the user, so whatever a user asks for, or a prompt injection makes the agent ask for, is allowed.In-scope ai-agent technical assets that act for users, through an incoming communication link with the identity end-user or from a caller used by humans (other than devops links), and reach a technical asset (other than an llm) processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with the identity service-account or workload, either directly or through the tools of an mcp-server technical asset.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the most sensitive technical asset the agent reaches with its own identity. The attack is likely when the agent takes untrusted input, and unlikely otherwise.
Container Base Image Backdooring
container-baseimage-backdooring		TamperingWhen a technical asset is built using container technologies, Base Image Backdooring risks might arise where base images and other layers used contain vulnerable components or backdoors.In-scope technical assets running as containers, other than external entities. To track the risks of all containers at once, use the risk tracking key container-baseimage-backdooring@*.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets.
Container Platform Escape
container-platform-escape		Elevation of PrivilegeContainer platforms are especially interesting targets for attackers as they host big parts of a containerized runtime infrastructure. When not configured and operated with security best practices in mind, attackers might exploit a vulnerability inside an container and escape towards the platform as highly privileged users. These scenarios might give attackers capabilities to attack every other container as owning the container platform (via container escape attacks) equals to owning every container.In-scope container platforms.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the technical asset itself and of the data assets processed.
Cross-Account Takeover
cross-account-takeover		Elevation of PrivilegeCloud accounts, subscriptions, projects and VPCs isolate workloads and tenants from each other. Access from one of them into another (account A to account B) is granted by cross-account roles, trust policies or resource policies, and a misconfigured grant (too broad principals or rights, or no condition on the calling account) breaks that isolation.Communication links into in-scope technical assets from technical assets in another cloud account, i.e. where the innermost trust boundaries of type network-cloud-provider around the source and the target differ.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the target technical asset itself and of the data assets it processes and stores. The likelihood rises when the source or the target is multi-tenant, as another tenant can then try to abuse the cross-account access.
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
cross-site-request-forgery		SpoofingWhen a web application is accessed via web protocols Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) risks might arise.In-scope web applications accessed via typical web access protocols by a caller used by humans or a browser, directly or through technical assets forwarding the traffic, like load balancers, reverse proxies and WAFs. Requests of other callers, like a backend or a batch job, come from no browser a forged request could use, and are skipped.The risk rating depends on the integrity rating of the data sent across the communication link. The attack is very likely, likely for DevOps usage, and unlikely when the link is authenticated with a token (token, short-lived-token or long-lived-token), which a browser does not send on its own like a cookie.
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
cross-site-scripting		TamperingFor each web application Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) risks might arise. In terms of the overall risk level take other applications running on the same domain into account as well.In-scope web applications.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed in the web application.
Direct IT/OT Communication
direct-it-ot-communication		Elevation of PrivilegeControllers, field devices, HMIs, SCADA servers and engineering workstations of an industrial control system belong into control zones that IT assets reach only through an industrial DMZ. A direct communication link between an IT asset and an asset of a control zone lets attackers who compromise the IT side, which is far more exposed, move straight into the control of the physical process.In-scope OT technical assets (plc, rtu, safety-controller, field-device, hmi, scada-server, engineering-workstation) with a communication link, in either direction, with a technical asset that is neither an OT asset nor in the industrial DMZ (a historian or an asset tagged with industrial-dmz).The risk rating depends on the integrity and availability of the OT asset, and is the highest for safety controllers. The attack is very likely when the other asset is on the internet, and likely otherwise.
DoS-risky Access Across Trust-Boundary
dos-risky-access-across-trust-boundary		Denial of ServiceAssets accessed across trust boundaries with critical or mission-critical availability rating are more prone to Denial-of-Service (DoS) risks.In-scope technical assets (excluding load-balancer) with availability rating of critical or higher which have incoming data-flows across a network trust-boundary (excluding devops usage).Matching technical assets with availability rating of critical or higher are at low risk. When the availability rating is mission-critical and neither a VPN nor IP filter for the incoming data-flow nor redundancy for the asset is applied, the risk-rating is considered medium.
Denial of Service by Encryption Key Deletion
encryption-key-deletion		Denial of ServiceData in cloud storage encrypted with a key from a cloud key management service (like AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault or Google Cloud KMS) can only be decrypted as long as the key exists. Deleting the key, by mistake or by an attacker with enough rights, makes the data permanently unusable.In-scope encrypted cloud technical assets (residing in cloud trust boundaries or tagged with cloud provider tags) storing data assets, which are either tagged as encrypted with a key from a cloud key management service (aws:kms, azure:keyvault, gcp:kms on the asset, a trust boundary around it or its shared runtime) or communicate with a cloud vault or hsm asset. Key stores themselves are excluded.The risk rating depends on the availability rating of the technical asset itself and of the data assets stored, as the deletion destroys the data but does not disclose it.
Excessive Agency
excessive-agency		Elevation of PrivilegeAn AI agent decides on its own which tools to call and with which arguments. An agent that can change critical systems, directly or through the tools of an MCP server, without a human approving the change, does whatever a prompt injection, a hallucination or a misunderstanding makes it do.In-scope ai-agent technical assets with a non-readonly communication link to a technical asset (other than an llm) processing or storing data rated at least as critical in integrity, either directly or through the tools of an mcp-server technical asset. Agents and links tagged with human-in-the-loop are skipped.The risk rating depends on the integrity rating of the technical asset the agent can change. The attack is likely when the agent takes untrusted input, and unlikely otherwise.
Human Use of Machine Identity
human-use-of-machine-identity		RepudiationPeople who call a service with the account of a machine, like an administrator using the credentials of a service account or a client that ships with an API key of its own, act without an identity of theirs. The service cannot tell them apart, nor require a second factor or end their access when they leave, and the secret gets copied to wherever they work.In-scope technical assets processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with an incoming communication link that is not process-local, from a caller used by humans, whose identity is service-account or workload.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed or stored by the target. The attack is likely, as secrets in the hands of people leak easily.
Incomplete Model
incomplete-model		Information DisclosureWhen the threat model contains unknown technologies or transfers data over unknown protocols, this is an indicator for an incomplete model.All technical assets and communication links with technology type or protocol type specified as unknown.low
Insecure Control Protocol
insecure-control-protocol		TamperingMost industrial control protocols, like Modbus, DNP3, S7comm, EtherNet/IP or PROFINET, were designed for closed networks: a controller or field device executes every command it receives, without checking who sent it or whether it was changed on the way. Anyone who can send packets to it can write setpoints and outputs, stop it or download a new program.In-scope controllers (plc, rtu, safety-controller) and field-device technical assets with an incoming non-readonly communication link over an industrial control protocol without a secure variant in use (all of them except modbus-security, dnp3-encrypted and opc-ua-encrypted).The risk rating depends on the integrity and availability of the controlled process, and is the highest for safety controllers. The attack is very likely when the sender is on the internet, likely when it is an IT asset, reaches IT or calls across a network trust boundary, and unlikely otherwise.
Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
insecure-inter-agent-communication		SpoofingAn AI agent takes the messages of another agent as tasks to act on. When it cannot verify which agent sent a message, because the link is not authenticated or only with a static secret, or cannot rely on the message being unchanged, because the link is not encrypted, anyone who reaches the link can make it act, and a prompt injection in one agent passes on to the next.Communication links that are not process-local between ai-agent technical assets, into an in-scope agent, whose authentication is none, credentials, session-id or long-lived-token, or whose protocol is not encrypted, when the receiving agent processes data rated at least as confidential or critical or can change such an asset, directly or through the tools of an mcp-server technical asset.The risk rating depends on what the receiving agent can do: the most sensitive data it processes or asset it can change. The attack is likely across a network trust boundary, and unlikely otherwise. The rules on missing authentication, long-lived credentials and unencrypted communication may report the same link for the data it carries.
Kubernetes API Write Access
kubernetes-api-write-access		Elevation of PrivilegeA workload whose service account may change resources through the API of its cluster, even narrowly, like creating pods, reading secrets or patching deployments, hands that power to whoever compromises the workload: a pod created with a mounted host path, or a secret read, opens the rest of the cluster.Communication links that are not readonly and not process-local to a container-platform technical asset from a technical asset that is not used by humans, where either is in scope. Links of devops usage, like deployments, are skipped.The risk rating depends on the most sensitive of the platform, the workload and the technical assets sharing a runtime with the workload. The attack is likely when the workload is on the internet or talks to the internet, and unlikely otherwise.
LDAP-Injection
ldap-injection		TamperingWhen an LDAP server is accessed LDAP-Injection risks might arise. The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the LDAP server itself and of the data assets processed.In-scope clients accessing LDAP servers via typical LDAP access protocols.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the LDAP server itself and of the data assets processed.
Long-Lived Credentials
long-lived-credentials		SpoofingPasswords of service accounts, API keys and personal access tokens stay valid for months or for good. Once one leaks, from a repository, a log, a build system or a laptop, it lets anyone in until someone notices and rotates it.In-scope technical assets processing or storing data rated at least as confidential or critical with an incoming communication link that is not process-local and is authenticated with long-lived-token, or with credentials by a caller not used by humans, unless the identity of the link is workload. Links authenticated with token are skipped, as the lifetime of the token is not modelled.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed or stored by the target. The attack is likely when the caller is on the internet, is used by humans or calls across a network trust boundary, where secrets leak more easily, and unlikely otherwise.
Missing AI Guardrail
missing-ai-guardrail		Elevation of PrivilegeA guardrail screens what reaches a language model or an agent, and what comes back from it, for prompt injection, jailbreaks and data that must not pass, independently of the model. Without one, the instructions of the system prompt are the only defense, and a model follows whatever content convinces it.In-scope llm and ai-agent technical assets that untrusted content reaches (as for prompt injection) through a communication link that no guardrail screens. A link is screened when it comes from an ai-guardrail technical asset, or when the model or agent is one itself or has a link to one. Links from other language models and agents are skipped, as the rule reports a missing guardrail where the content first reaches a model.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed by the model or agent. The attack is likely when the model or agent talks to the internet directly, and unlikely otherwise.
Missing AI Monitoring
missing-ai-monitoring		RepudiationWhat an AI agent or a language model does depends on what it reads, so it cannot be tested in full before it runs. Without a record of its prompts, its tool calls and its answers in a monitoring system, nobody sees a prompt injection, an agent going astray or a model that drifts, nor can tell afterwards what it did.In-scope ai-agent technical assets, and in-scope llm technical assets not on the internet (self-hosted models), with no communication link to or from a monitoring technical asset.The risk rating depends on the sensitivity of the data processed by the agent or model. The attack is likely when the agent or model takes untrusted content, and unlikely otherwise.
Missing Authentication
missing-authentication		Elevation of PrivilegeTechnical assets (especially multi-tenant systems) should authenticate incoming requests when the asset processes sensitive data. In-scope technical assets (except load-balancer, reverse-proxy, service-registry, waf, ids, and ips and in-process calls) should authenticate incoming requests when the asset processes sensitive data. This is especially the case for all multi-tenant assets (there even non-sensitive ones).
